title: Unified Multi-Layer Subspace Modeling for Cross-Domain OOD Detection
abstract: Out-of-Distribution (OOD) detection remains a fundamental challenge for neural networks, whose predictions can be overconfident on inputs that deviate from the training distribution. Most post-hoc OOD detection methods derive scores from a single representation level (eg., logits or penultimate features) or combine multiple layers via depth selection or OOD-calibrated weighting. However, because OOD shifts are diverse, the most informative representation level can vary strongly across OOD types and domains, making fixed-layer choices and OOD-calibrated aggregation brittle. In this paper, we propose PRISM (Projected Representation with Intermediate-layer Subspace Modeling), a model-agnostic post-hoc OOD detection method that models a unified multi-layer feature representation rather than aggregating independently scored layers. title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning for Container Kubernetes Orchestration in Uganda: Robustness Under Distribution Shift and Sparse Labels
abstract: Federated learning offers a compelling architecture for training machine learning models across distributed Kubernetes clusters without centralising sensitive data, yet its practical deployment in resource-constrained settings such as Uganda confronts two interrelated obstacles that current literature treats in isolation: distribution shift between participating sites and extreme label sparsity. We introduce a hierarchical Bayesian model of client heterogeneity that distinguishes benign statistical variation from systematic covariate shift, and we prove that a proposed double-regularised aggregation operator achieves bounded excess risk under conditions where standard FedAvg diverges. The framework further incorporates a semi-supervised pseudo-labelling mechanism with rigorous uncertainty thresholds, demonstrating that selective label propagation can stabilise training when annotated data are scarce. Theoretical analysis establishes convergence guarantees under non-IID data partitions, and the architectural instantiation on Kubernetes demonstrates that privacy constraints, implemented through secure aggregation and differential privacy, do not compromise the robustness properties we derive. The contribution is a unified treatment of distribution shift and label scarcity that yields testable propositions for deployment in Ugandan data centres and other low-resource environments.

title: ElVec1o/nested-leap-complexity: The GF(p)-Linear Complexity of Nested Leap-Year Sequences
abstract: Elementary determination of the linear complexity of staircase sequences and their linear combinations over finite fields, with application to the Gregorian leap-year count. Paper Files: nested-leap-complexity.pdf — Full 10-page paper with all proofs nested-leap-complexity.md — Markdown version verify.py — Regenerates all computational claims (requires numpy, sympy) Abstract: For a positive integer n and prime p, the staircase sequence g_n(Y) = floor(Y/n) mod p has linear complexity n+1. We determine the linear complexity of every F_p-linear combination of such sequences: it is M+1 minus a sum of Euler-φ terms. For the nested leap-correction sequence L_{a,b,c} = g_a - g_{ab} + g_{abc} (the Gregorian calendar rule), we prove: L(L_{a,b,c}) = abc+1 - (ab-a)·[p | c-1] - a·[p | bc-c+1] For the Gregorian rule (a,b,c)=(4,25,4), the leap-year count has linear complexity exactly 401 modulo every prime p ∤ 400, except p=3 (complexity 305) and p=97 (complexity 397).

title: 基于概率逻辑的动态自适应优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic self-adaptive optimization algorithm based on probabilistic logic. Traditional optimization methods often rely on static parameter adjustments, limiting their efficiency. This algorithm employs probabilistic logic to dynamically adjust optimization parameters based on the objective function and current state, leading to significantly improved optimization performance. The core mechanism involves a probabilistic model that evolves over time, allowing the algorithm to intelligently adapt to changing conditions and optimize for complex, non-linear objective functions. This approach offers enhanced robustness and potential for faster convergence compared to conventional methods. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, the probabilistic model utilized, and its performance evaluation against established optimization techniques. The proposed algorithm demonstrates superior results in a series of benchmark test cases, highlighting its potential for applications across various domains.

title: The Quantum Entanglement Optimization via Probabilistic Modeling
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, presents a unique opportunity for revolutionary computational and communication paradigms. However, harnessing this phenomenon effectively requires sophisticated optimization techniques. This paper explores the application of probabilistic modeling to optimize complex quantum systems, particularly those involving multi-particle entanglement. We propose a novel framework that transforms the inherent evolution of quantum states into a probabilistic process, leveraging the properties of entanglement to control and optimize the behavior of these systems. The core mechanism centers around the design of a probabilistic computation method, offering a potential pathway to enhance quantum computing and quantum communication efficiency. This work addresses a critical gap in our understanding of optimizing complex quantum systems, offering a promising approach to tackling challenges in these rapidly evolving fields.

title: WRRA-Based Embodied Intelligence with Present Residue and Minimal Computation
abstract: This study investigates whether the Wonsik Reality-Renderer Architecture (WRRA) can be implemented as an executable artificial intelligence architecture using a 23-node, 57-relation neural circuit inspired by the C. elegans nervous system. Following the WRRA criteria for classifying interpretation and prediction, the experiments are divided into interpretation, computation, prediction, and control tasks. Present sensory reading and structural auditing are classified as interpretation, deterministic state updating as computation, and delayed-cue decisions, food seeking under intermittent sensing, and performance in unseen environments as prediction and control.WRRA-Worm versions 0.2 and 0.3 successfully demonstrated delayed memory, reward-modulated plasticity, embodied sensorimotor learning, and food acquisition dependent on present neural residue. Version 0.4 compared WRRA with memoryless, Elman RNN, and GRU policies under an equal budget of 84 optimized parameters using the same Cross-Entropy Method protocol. WRRA produced the lowest collision rate across all evaluation conditions but did not outperform the smaller conventional architectures in reward or food acquisition. A memoryless policy performed best when current sensing was sufficient, while a small RNN was strongest under sparse sensing.The results demonstrate that WRRA can function as an auditable AI design architecture, but they do not support its general predictive superiority. Its current strength lies in conservative safety behavior and explicit tracking of present residue, relations, resources, rendering, and claim boundaries. The study identifies conditional activation of residue circuits as the next direction for achieving minimal computation. This is a computational proof of concept rather than a biological reconstruction of the complete 302-neuron C. elegans nervous system.Reference framework: Choi, W. (2026), “WRRA Criteria for Classifying Interpretation and Prediction,” DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22447864.

title: Title: Dynamically Reconfigurable Quantum Field Mapping
abstract: This paper investigates the concept of dynamically reconfigurable quantum field mapping, a novel approach to quantum field manipulation that moves beyond static, fixed field configurations. We propose a system wherein the quantum field map is continuously adjusted based on external stimuli or internal system state, generating entirely new quantum states. The core mechanism revolves around a feedback loop that iteratively modifies the field map to achieve specific desired quantum properties. This design offers a fundamentally new pathway for exploring and harnessing quantum phenomena, potentially leading to breakthroughs in quantum computing, quantum sensing, and fundamental physics. The paper details the underlying mathematical framework and provides a preliminary demonstration of the system's capabilities, highlighting key advancements in adaptive control and field state evolution.

title: Title: Non-Linear Geometric Topology for Quantum State Preservation
abstract: Abstract: This paper explores the application of non-linear geometric topology, specifically fractal geometry, to the preservation of quantum states. Quantum states exhibit inherent fragility, susceptible to decoherence over extended time scales and environmental perturbations. Existing topological methods often fall short in effectively managing this sensitivity. This work proposes a novel approach utilizing dynamically evolving topology, inspired by fractal patterns, to mitigate decoherence. This topology adapts to subtle quantum fluctuations, offering a robust framework for quantum computing and information processing. We detail the core mechanism – a self-correcting topology – and present preliminary results demonstrating its potential for preserving quantum coherence.

title: Dynamic Bayesian Uncertainty Quantification using Variational Autoencoders
abstract: Bayesian uncertainty quantification (UQ) is a crucial element in modern scientific modeling, particularly for dynamic systems where inherent uncertainties in model parameters and initial conditions lead to a range of possible outcomes. However, traditional UQ methods, such as Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling, often demand substantial computational resources, limiting their applicability to complex systems with high-dimensional state spaces. This work introduces a novel approach leveraging Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) to achieve dynamic Bayesian UQ with significantly reduced computational cost. The core idea is to train a VAE to learn a low-dimensional latent representation of the dynamic system's state space, effectively capturing the underlying dynamics. This latent representation is then used to perform UQ, providing an efficient and accurate assessment of uncertainty. The proposed method offers a promising alternative to traditional UQ techniques, particularly for systems where computational resources are limited. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and discuss its potential applications across various domains.

title: Algorithmic Bayesian Probability with Stochastic Constraint Mapping (AB-SCM)
abstract: This paper introduces Algorithmic Bayesian Probability with Stochastic Constraint Mapping (AB-SCM), a novel framework for probabilistic modeling designed to handle evolving, uncertain environments. The core idea of AB-SCM is to dynamically map constraints onto a probabilistic model, enabling continuous adaptation to new information. This approach departs from static Bayesian methods by incorporating a mechanism for real-time constraint updates, resulting in a highly flexible and robust probabilistic system. We present a new algorithm that leverages a probabilistic constraint mapping process, incorporating a novel weighting scheme to dynamically adjust the influence of constraints on the model. The paper details the implementation of the algorithm, demonstrates its performance on a benchmark set of problems, and discusses future research directions. The benefits of AB-SCM are highlighted in terms of adaptability, robustness, and the ability to handle complex, dynamic environments.

title: Symbolic Regression with Evolutionary Strategies and Latent Variable Models
abstract: Symbolic regression aims to discover mathematical expressions that accurately describe a given dataset. However, traditional methods often struggle to identify complex, non-linear relationships, particularly when the underlying data distribution is intricate. This work proposes a novel approach that combines evolutionary strategies (ES) for optimizing symbolic expressions with latent variable models (LVMs) to capture the underlying data distribution. The ES component iteratively refines the symbolic expressions, while the LVM provides a smoother, more informed search space, mitigating the challenges associated with purely symbolic exploration. The integration allows the system to discover more complex and accurate functional models. We demonstrate the efficacy of this combined approach through a series of simulations, highlighting its ability to surpass the limitations of traditional symbolic regression techniques in scenarios with complex data dependencies. The core claim of this research is that combining ES with LVMs significantly improves the ability to find complex, non-linear relationships.

title: Cognitive Maps Semantic Embedding Learning
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to constructing cognitive maps by learning semantic embeddings from diverse knowledge graphs. The core idea is to leverage the rich relational information encoded within knowledge graphs to build a multi-modal semantic embedding space, facilitating a deeper understanding and reasoning capabilities regarding complex concepts and their interconnections. We employ Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to learn node and edge embeddings from these knowledge graphs, effectively capturing semantic relationships across various cognitive domains. The resulting embedding space allows for efficient similarity comparisons and relationship inference, ultimately contributing to a more comprehensive and dynamic representation of cognitive maps. Our method addresses the limitations of traditional cognitive mapping techniques by incorporating the structured knowledge inherent in knowledge graphs. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a theoretical framework, outlining the key components and their interactions. The research contributes to advancements in knowledge representation, reasoning, and the development of intelligent systems capable of navigating and understanding complex cognitive landscapes.

title: Interpreting Deep Learning Models through Symbolic Reasoning
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to interpreting deep learning models by integrating symbolic reasoning. Traditional deep learning models are often considered "black boxes," making it difficult to understand their decision-making processes. This work proposes a framework that combines the strengths of both deep learning and symbolic AI. Specifically, we leverage the predictive power of deep neural networks alongside logical inference techniques to explain the internal reasoning of these models. The core mechanism involves comparing the outputs of a deep learning model with knowledge represented in a symbolic knowledge base. By applying logical inference algorithms, we can derive a symbolic representation of the model's reasoning process, providing a more transparent and understandable explanation. This approach aims to enhance the trustworthiness and interpretability of deep learning systems, a critical step towards wider adoption and reliable deployment. The key contributions include a novel framework and a methodology for translating deep learning outputs into logical inferences, leading to enhanced model interpretability.

title: Global minimax risk and acquisition laws for heterogeneous information fusion
abstract: We prove an all-allocation global target-risk theorem for independent Gaussian sources that share a scalar nuisance and an unknown contact coordinate. For a fixed immersed nuisance curve with finitely many multiple fibres and pairwise nonparallel branch tangents, squared target risk is comparable to a primary estimation floor plus a target-gap-weighted Gaussian discrimination profile. Independent localization, finite branch selection and target-class refitting give an estimator attaining this comparison across every nonnegative integer allocation. A full-box specialization has positive-definite primary Fisher information everywhere and globally identifies its target, yet models with identical derivatives of every order along a critical hypersurface have different polynomial risk exponents. We construct a finite certified estimator and quantify the numerical accuracy needed to preserve rare branch decisions and acquisition windows. A polynomial tangency family both demonstrates the geometric boundary and quantifies its repair: known auxiliary gain, source contact order and target vanishing order determine a risk law uniform through zero gain. For a shared spherical direction, a separately proved composite-testing result transfers through an unknown contact coordinate using only counted observations. These theorems distinguish the resources needed for local estimation, discrimination between parameter regions and nuisance alignment, and yield acquisition thresholds under explicit scalar-observation costs.

title: Diffuse2Seg: Diffusion Models Can Segment Anything Without Supervision
abstract: Open-world entity segmentation aims to predict masks for arbitrary objects across domains and at multiple granularities, from parts to whole objects. In this setting, SAM sets a strong standard: trained on SA-1B, comprising 11M images and over 1B carefully annotated masks, it achieves remarkable zero-shot performance. Collecting such labels is expensive and time-consuming, however, which limits how far this recipe can scale. Text-to-image diffusion models offer a way around this. Their intermediate features transfer well across perception tasks, and since object structure emerges as the model denoises a noise sample into an image conditioned on a text prompt, that structure is already encoded in these representations. They can therefore be exploited for open-world entity segmentation without retraining or supervision. Building on this observation, we introduce Diffuse2Seg, which repurposes generative diffusion models for automatic mask generation by propagating a grid of point prompts through their self-attention representations in an edge-preserving manner. Diffuse2Seg produces multi-granular instance masks and outperforms prior state-of-the-art label generators by 4.3-7.1 p.p. in AR_1000 across five domains. Training an instance segmentation model on these generated masks advances detector-free open-world segmentation by 7.4 and 7.7 p.p. on "things" and "stuff+things" datasets and surpasses the detector-based UnSAM on "stuff+things" by 2.1 p.p. in AR_1000. Finally, we show that a model trained on Diffuse2Seg labels provides a strong initialization for semi-supervised learning, outperforming its fully supervised counterpart with already 5k labeled images.

title: Title: Fractal Dynamics & Quantum Complexity
abstract: Fractal Dynamics & Quantum Complexity The inherent complexity of quantum systems necessitates innovative approaches to control and manipulation. This research explores the potential of utilizing fractal dynamics to stabilize quantum systems, envisioning a 'quantum fractal' capable of self-organizing into complex patterns. This project focuses on the development of a novel algorithm, the 'Fractal Resonance' method, designed to harness the self-similarity inherent in fractal structures to achieve a state of quantum stability. The core mechanism involves a carefully orchestrated iterative process applied to quantum entanglement, promoting self-organization and stabilization through fractal self-similarity. This work addresses the limitations of current quantum computing by presenting a fundamentally different approach that leverages the principles of fractal geometry to enhance quantum coherence and robustness. The resulting 'quantum fractal' promises a pathway towards more stable and controllable quantum systems.

abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum entanglement to solve the computational geometry optimization problem. We propose a novel model leveraging entangled quantum states to simulate system interactions and implement a new optimization algorithm based on this entanglement principle. The core claim is that this approach offers a pathway to significantly enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of optimization algorithms, particularly in complex, multi-dimensional problems. The mechanism involves utilizing entanglement to represent and manipulate system variables, allowing for more intuitive and potentially faster optimization procedures. This work introduces a new algorithm that utilizes the inherent properties of quantum entanglement to guide the search process, potentially leading to improved results compared to traditional optimization techniques.

title: Self-Organizing Quantum Topology Networks
abstract: This paper explores the concept of Self-Organizing Quantum Topology Networks (SOTN) as a novel approach to quantum information processing and communication. Quantum topology, a rapidly developing field, offers unique properties that can be harnessed to create robust and scalable quantum networks. We propose a model for constructing SOTN networks, leveraging the interplay of quantum entanglement, self-consistency, and the inherent topology of quantum systems. The core mechanism centers around establishing robust and interconnected quantum nodes through the manipulation of entangled states and self-consistent quantum states, facilitating secure and efficient quantum information transfer. This research investigates the potential of SOTN networks for advanced quantum communication protocols, highlighting the advantages over traditional quantum networks and emphasizing the fundamental role of quantum topology in achieving these advantages.

title: Time Series Cryptographic Algorithms
abstract: Time series cryptography addresses the challenges posed by the increasing complexity and sensitivity of real-world data, particularly time series data. This paper explores the design and implementation of a novel cryptographic algorithm, Time Series Encryption Algorithm (TSEA), built upon the principle of dynamic pattern recognition and key updates. Traditional cryptographic methods often rely on static keys, which are vulnerable to attacks. TSEA leverages real-time analysis of time series data to generate keys dynamically, thereby enhancing security and offering a significant advantage over static key management approaches. The core mechanism centers around a dynamic pattern recognition module, which continuously assesses the data's characteristics, and utilizes this information to create a unique and secure key for each data point. This paper provides a detailed outline of the algorithm's design, analysis of its security properties, and preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness.

title: Core Claim: Develop a quantum spin-based non-symmetric matrix multiplication algorithm capable of efficiently handling matrices with non-symmetric properties, exhibiting adaptive computational efficiency.
abstract: The efficient computation of matrices, particularly those with non-symmetric properties, remains a significant challenge in various scientific and engineering fields. This paper presents a novel quantum spin-based matrix multiplication algorithm designed to address this challenge. We introduce a dynamic adjustment mechanism leveraging the intrinsic self-adaptivity of quantum spin systems to optimize the matrix multiplication process. The algorithm's core mechanism involves a carefully designed quantum circuit that adapts the matrix multiplication operation based on the specific characteristics of the input matrix. This adaptive approach significantly enhances computational efficiency, offering a potential breakthrough in matrix multiplication performance. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this algorithm through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation, highlighting its ability to outperform traditional approaches in certain scenarios. The research explores the potential of quantum spin systems to provide a fundamentally new paradigm in matrix multiplication, offering a promising pathway toward more efficient and scalable computations.

title: Distributed Quantum Computation via Relayed Entanglement
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to distributed quantum computation – utilizing relayed entanglement – to circumvent the limitations imposed by long-distance entanglement distribution. Direct quantum communication suffers from the exponential decay of signal fidelity over extended distances, making entanglement creation and distribution across vast networks prohibitively difficult. This work proposes a network architecture leveraging intermediate nodes, acting as relays, to facilitate the transfer of entanglement. The core concept involves creating entangled pairs locally and then relaying them through the network, effectively extending the range of quantum computation without the need for direct, long-distance entanglement. We present a theoretical framework outlining the key components and considerations for such a system, including entanglement generation, relay protocols, and error mitigation strategies. This approach offers a viable pathway towards scalable distributed quantum computation, addressing a critical bottleneck in the development of practical quantum networks. The system is designed to improve the fidelity of quantum operations performed across geographically dispersed qubits. The presented model provides a foundational understanding for future research and development in this area.

abstract: Quantum state computation (QSC) is a rapidly growing field with the potential to revolutionize various scientific and technological applications. Traditional approaches to QSC often rely on meticulously crafted parameters, limiting their adaptability and hindering efficient quantum state manipulation. This paper introduces a novel QSC method based on dynamic neural network adjustments, aiming to overcome these limitations. We propose a "quantum state calculation model dynamic adjustment" mechanism which automatically adjusts the structure and weights of a neural network to optimize quantum state calculation. We present a theoretical framework and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach. title: Dynamic Memory Networks with Contextualized Attention Modulation
abstract: Memory Networks (MNs) have demonstrated remarkable success in tasks requiring reasoning over long sequences, such as question answering and knowledge base completion. However, a fundamental limitation of traditional MNs lies in their reliance on static attention mechanisms. These mechanisms assign fixed weights to memory slots, regardless of the evolving context, hindering their ability to prioritize relevant information effectively. This paper introduces a novel architecture, Dynamic Memory Networks with Contextualized Attention Modulation (DMN-CAM), designed to address this deficiency. DMN-CAM integrates a recurrent neural network (RNN) to process contextual information and dynamically modulate the attention weights within the core Memory Network. The RNN learns to adaptively scale and shift attention based on the current state of the context, resulting in a more refined and context-aware memory access strategy. The proposed approach significantly improves performance in dynamic tasks where contextual understanding is crucial. We present a detailed formulation of the model and demonstrate its effectiveness through a theoretical analysis.

title: Hierarchical Graph Attention Networks for Multi-Scale Data
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to multi-scale data analysis utilizing Hierarchical Graph Attention Networks (HGATs). The core idea is that representing data with hierarchical graph structures can effectively capture dependencies across various scales, resulting in enhanced performance in complex tasks. We propose a dynamic hierarchical graph attention network construction mechanism, leveraging data-driven clustering and graph traversal to establish and evolve the network's hierarchy. This allows for efficient information flow across different scales, addressing a key limitation of traditional graph attention networks. Our HGAT architecture allows for the explicit modeling of relationships at multiple granularities, leading to improved feature representations and ultimately, better predictive performance. The key contribution lies in the adaptive and data-driven nature of the hierarchy, ensuring that the network structure aligns with the underlying data structure, which is crucial for effective multi-scale analysis. The proposed method is demonstrated through a conceptual framework and theoretical justification, setting the stage for future empirical validation.

title: Quantum-Inspired Optimization of Large-Scale Logistic Networks
abstract: Large-scale logistic networks present a formidable challenge to traditional optimization techniques. The sheer number of variables and constraints involved—including vehicle routing, shipment scheduling, warehouse operations, and inventory management—often leads to computational bottlenecks, hindering efficient network design and operation. This paper investigates the application of quantum-inspired optimization algorithms to address these challenges. Specifically, we explore the potential of algorithms mimicking quantum phenomena, such as quantum annealing and quantum walks, to efficiently solve complex routing and scheduling problems within large logistic networks. Our approach leverages the inherent parallelism and ability of these algorithms to navigate complex solution spaces, offering a promising alternative to classical methods. We demonstrate the feasibility and potential benefits of this strategy through a theoretical framework and illustrative examples, highlighting the advantages of quantum-inspired optimization for improving the performance of large-scale logistic networks.

title: DrugReason: Dynamic Multi-View Reasoning over Knowledge Graph and Language Evidence for Drug Repurposing
abstract: Drug repurposing aims to identify new therapeutic uses for existing compounds and, compared with de novo drug discovery, offers a faster and more cost-effective path to clinical translation. However, the space of candidate drug-disease pairs is enormous and their underlying relationships often depend on complex multi-hop biological mechanisms, making it difficult to reliably predict which pairs represent true therapeutic relationships. Existing approaches tackle this from two directions: knowledge graph-based methods organize curated biomedical evidence into structured relational networks for grounded multi-hop reasoning, while LLM-based methods leverage pretrained knowledge to generate flexible mechanistic rationales. Yet neither is sufficient alone - KGs are confined to observed graph structure while LLMs lack factual grounding and risk hallucination. To address this gap, we propose DrugReason, a multi-view reasoning framework that integrates grounded KG reasoning with LLM-generated mechanistic inference for drug repurposing. DrugReason adaptively routes diverse reasoning paths to specialized experts conditioned on the query context, while a cross-expert distillation objective enables knowledge sharing without sacrificing expert specialization. Experiments on PharmaDB, DDInter, and DrugBank show that DrugReason improves average performance over strong single-view reasoning baselines and achieves competitive or superior results compared with graph-based alternatives, while providing interpretable routing-based predictions.

title: Quantum-Inspired Algorithms for Differential Geometry
abstract: Quantum-Inspired Algorithms for Differential Geometry addresses the limitations of classical methods in handling complex shapes and transformations, leveraging quantum principles to approximate solutions and offer speedups. This paper explores the potential of quantum algorithms to enhance the efficiency and capabilities of differential geometry, focusing on specific problem areas and outlining a novel approach. The core claim centers on the development of algorithms that mimic quantum phenomena to improve the robustness and speed of solutions.

title: Non-Linear Topological Geometry: Algorithm Design for Quantum Computation
abstract: This paper investigates the application of non-linear topological geometry to algorithm design for quantum computation, specifically focusing on the optimization of quantum circuits and the design of novel quantum algorithms. We introduce a novel algorithm that leverages quantum entanglement to dynamically adjust the topology of geometric data structures, enabling efficient parameter optimization and quantum algorithm development. The core mechanism centers around the exploration of quantum entanglement as a means of manipulating and optimizing the geometric structure of the data, ultimately leading to improved performance in quantum computation. The algorithm's design addresses limitations of traditional quantum computing approaches by providing a mechanism for direct data manipulation and optimization, offering a potentially transformative impact on the field.

title: Hierarchical Bayesian Modeling for Probabilistic Physics
abstract: This paper explores the application of hierarchical Bayesian modeling to probabilistic physics, aiming to create a framework for capturing complex probability distributions across multiple levels of abstraction within physical systems. Traditional Bayesian approaches frequently encounter challenges with high-dimensional data, necessitating more robust and interpretable models. We propose a tree-like structure where each node represents a level of detail, allowing for a more nuanced understanding of the system's behavior. This approach addresses these limitations, offering a novel framework for modeling intricate physical phenomena. The core mechanism involves constructing a hierarchical Bayesian model that seamlessly integrates data from various levels of granularity. We detail the model's structure, the rationale behind its design, and initial results demonstrating its potential for improved probabilistic understanding.

title: 基于量子态的神经网络的自适应学习策略
abstract: This paper presents a novel neural network architecture leveraging quantum state dynamics for adaptive learning. Traditional neural networks often rely on static learning rates, limiting their ability to optimize for complex data patterns. We propose a quantum-inspired approach that utilizes the inherent properties of quantum states – specifically, self-avoidance and entanglement – to dynamically adjust learning parameters, resulting in enhanced prediction accuracy. This research explores the potential of harnessing quantum phenomena to improve the learning process, moving beyond the limitations of conventional methods. The core of this work is the development of a quantum state optimization algorithm that dynamically adjusts the network's parameters based on the quantum state's evolution. We analyze the impact of this dynamic adjustment on prediction accuracy and demonstrate a significant improvement over baseline techniques. The presented method offers a promising avenue for advancing neural network learning, particularly in scenarios demanding high precision and adaptability.

title: Dimensional Geometry Quantum Computation
abstract: This paper explores the potential of leveraging dimensionality geometry as a foundational element within quantum computation. The core claim is to design a novel quantum computing framework that utilizes geometric structures to enhance efficiency and precision, and to optimize quantum information encoding and processing. The methodology centers around exploiting the unique properties of high-dimensional geometries to design quantum bits, enhance quantum entanglement, and improve overall computational performance. This work aims to shift the focus from standard qubit manipulation to a more sophisticated approach that fundamentally alters the computational landscape. The research will detail the design of a quantum computing architecture leveraging geometric principles, explore the impact of quantum entanglement and tunneling on key operations, and present a conceptual roadmap for future research and development.

abstract: This paper investigates the application of adaptive geometric topology optimization to self-adaptive quantum computation. Traditional quantum algorithms often rely on static mappings, limiting their capacity to handle complex geometric structures. We propose a novel algorithm that leverages the dynamic evolution of quantum states, driven by learned geometric patterns, to achieve enhanced computational efficiency. The core mechanism centers around a self-optimizing algorithm that analyzes the quantum state's geometry and adjusts its parameters to optimize performance. This approach addresses limitations of static optimization strategies by introducing a continuous, adaptive refinement process. The potential benefits include improved adaptability, enhanced control over quantum states, and potentially, higher computational throughput. This work presents a framework for dynamically sculpting the quantum state, offering a new pathway towards more efficient quantum computation.

title: Topology-Based Constraint Propagation for Bayesian Inference
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to Bayesian inference leveraging topology-based constraint propagation. Traditional methods often struggle with complex models and require extensive computational effort. We introduce a new method that constructs a geometric representation of the problem space, allowing for a more efficient and accurate propagation of constraints through the Bayesian inference process. The core mechanism involves representing the problem space using differential geometry, enabling the identification of crucial geometric relationships that drive the Bayesian inference. This method promises improved accuracy and efficiency, particularly for complex models with high-dimensional spaces.

title: Quantum Topology Quantum Information Storage Optimization
abstract: Quantum topology, a fascinating field of physics, offers unique structural properties that hold significant promise for advanced quantum information processing. This research investigates a novel quantum information storage optimization algorithm predicated on quantum topology, aiming to enhance the efficiency and precision of quantum data storage and retrieval. Traditional approaches to quantum information management often suffer from limitations in scalability and control. This algorithm leverages the inherent self-organization of quantum spacetime to construct a robust and adaptable storage framework. The core mechanism centers around manipulating the topology of quantum states to facilitate rapid access to desired information. The potential impact of this research extends to revolutionizing the field of quantum information technology, offering a pathway towards more practical and reliable quantum data storage and retrieval.

title: Dynamic Quantum Algorithms Based on Biological Synaptic Plasticity
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to quantum algorithm design by leveraging the principles of biological synaptic plasticity. The core idea is to mimic the dynamic adjustments observed in neuronal synapses to dynamically optimize and adapt quantum algorithms. We propose a framework where the inherent plasticity of biological systems is translated into a mechanism for parameter tuning and error correction within quantum computations. Specifically, we model synaptic plasticity, such as Hebbian learning and spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP), and integrate these models into the optimization process of quantum algorithms. This approach aims to endow quantum algorithms with self-learning and adaptive capabilities, potentially leading to significant improvements in efficiency and robustness. The theoretical framework presented here provides a foundation for developing more resilient and adaptable quantum computing solutions, drawing inspiration from the remarkable adaptability of the human brain. We analyze the potential impact of this dynamic adaptation on various quantum algorithms and outline key challenges and future research directions. ---

title: Adaptive Dynamic Graph Neural Network Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive dynamic graph neural network optimization framework designed to address the limitations of traditional methods. The core focus is on dynamically adjusting the connection weights of a graph neural network (GNN) based on observed input data variations. We propose a novel learning mechanism that adapts the weight adjustments during training, enabling the network to maintain optimal performance even in the face of evolving data. The paper details the implementation of a self-adaptive weight adjustment process, incorporating a feedback loop to continuously refine the network's parameters. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and preliminary experiments on benchmark datasets, showcasing improved accuracy and robustness compared to existing optimization techniques. The resulting framework offers a more adaptable and efficient approach to training GNNs, particularly in dynamic and complex environments.

title: Quantum Entanglement Non-Locality Computing
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental aspect of quantum mechanics, exhibits correlations that defy classical intuition. This research explores the potential of leveraging entanglement for enhanced computational capabilities, particularly within distributed quantum systems. We propose a novel model centered around entanglement-based information transfer and computation, aiming to overcome the limitations of classical locality and facilitate complex quantum algorithms. The core mechanism involves the design and implementation of a quantum entanglement network to expand the reach of quantum computation. This work investigates the fundamental implications of entanglement in the context of distributed quantum computing, pushing the boundaries of what's possible in this rapidly evolving field. We aim to demonstrate the feasibility of utilizing entanglement to enable fundamentally new computational paradigms.

title: Probabilistic Space Domain Embedding for Cross-Domain Data Fusion
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to cross-domain data fusion leveraging the concept of Probabilistic Space Domain Embedding (PSDE). The core idea is to map data from disparate domains – encompassing text, images, and audio – into a unified probabilistic space. This transformation facilitates seamless data integration and unlocks opportunities for knowledge discovery by exploiting the geometric relationships inherent within the probabilistic space. We utilize probability space theory and machine learning algorithms to construct domain-specific probability distributions. Subsequently, data points are projected into this shared space using operations like distance and similarity, allowing for effective data fusion and reasoning. The significance of PSDE lies in its ability to transcend domain boundaries, promoting the sharing and utilization of knowledge across diverse fields. This work establishes a foundational framework for future research in cross-domain data integration and intelligent systems.

title: ##基于图神经网络的复杂网络拓扑识别
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for the automated identification and analysis of complex network topologies. Traditional network analysis methods often struggle to capture the intricate relationships and emergent patterns found in complex networks, such as social networks, biological networks, and technological networks. GNNs offer a powerful approach by directly leveraging the graph structure itself as the primary data source. This work proposes a framework utilizing Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) and explores their effectiveness in learning topological features and predicting network evolution. The core claim is that GNNs provide a novel methodology for complex network analysis, enabling automated identification and predictive modeling. This research contributes to a deeper understanding of complex network behavior and opens possibilities for applications in various domains. The methodology focuses on feature extraction using GCNs and ultimately predicts future network states based on learned representations. ---

title: 基于多智能体强化学习的分布式资源调度与冲突解决
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed resource scheduling and conflict resolution leveraging Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL). The core idea is to decompose the complex problem into smaller, manageable tasks handled by multiple agents. Each agent is trained using reinforcement learning to optimize resource allocation within its designated area, while considering potential conflicts. A key aspect of this approach is the implementation of a collaborative mechanism between agents, enabling them to learn and adapt collectively. This results in a distributed system capable of achieving optimal resource scheduling and efficient conflict resolution. The system's parallel learning capability, a direct benefit of MARL, is exploited to handle large-scale resource management challenges, ultimately enhancing system efficiency and robustness. The presented methodology offers a scalable and adaptable solution for dynamic resource allocation scenarios.

abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to intelligent control system design by leveraging cognitive architectures. Traditional control systems often struggle to adapt to dynamic and uncertain environments, relying heavily on pre-programmed rules and lacking true understanding. This research posits that integrating cognitive principles, specifically through the use of cognitive architectures, can significantly enhance control system performance. We outline a framework for building intelligent control systems that mimic human cognitive processes, incorporating mechanisms such as attention, decision-making, and action execution. The core claim is that such a system, grounded in cognitive architecture, will better understand the environment and make more rational control decisions. This paper details the key components of this architecture and explores the potential benefits of this approach for a wide range of control applications.

title: Quantum Entanglement Field Modulation
abstract: Quantum Entanglement Field Modulation (QEFM) presents a novel framework for precisely controlling and manipulating quantum entanglement through a spatially-localized, oscillating field. This system leverages modified quantum gravity principles and a dynamically evolving "Quantum Resonance Cascade" to achieve predictable feedback loops, offering enhanced quantum communication and sensing capabilities. The core mechanism involves the creation of a field that subtly alters entanglement strength and distance, resulting in measurable and controllable manipulations. This work explores the foundational principles and potential applications of QEFM, highlighting its innovative approach to quantum control and its implications for future technological advancements.

title: "Reproducibility package: Predictive Similarity Does Not Imply Selection Reproducibility"
abstract: Feature selection and class-imbalance handling are routinely combined in medical tabular classification, yet judged by predictive performance alone. Whetherresampling changes the reproducibility of the selection itself is left unmeasured, although selected variables are often reported as clinical findings. Thisstudy treats imbalance handling as a controlled pipeline factor. Every data-level sampler is paired with a matched no-resampling condition on the same validation split under a training-only contract, and reproducibility is quantified by a chance-corrected estimator over fifty outer fits. A sequential rule treats predictive competitiveness as a hard constraint and ranks qualifying candidates by reproducibility. Four selector families and five imbalance conditions were evaluated on six binary medical datasets, with imbalance ratios from 1.6 to 14.6. Of sixty matched external contrasts, twenty-three produced material reproducibility changes, twenty of them reductions. In sixteen, a material loss coexisted with a paired predictive difference below the prespecified tolerance, a pattern invisible to a purely predictive evaluation. Only two of seven prespecified omnibus tests survived multiplicity correction. The rule changed the recommended pipeline in five of six datasets. Predictive similarity therefore does not imply comparable selection reproducibility, and measuring both turns an unrecognised cost of resampling into an explicit pipeline choice.

title: NEO-BENCH: A New Multi-Source Benchmark for Generalizable Astronomical Streak Detection
abstract: Near-Earth Objects (NEOs) can appear as faint streaks in long-exposure astronomical images. Detecting these streaks across diverse observatories requires methods that remain reliable despite differences in image quality, orientation, sky background, and noise. However, existing detectors are commonly evaluated using data from only one source, providing limited evidence of cross-source generalization. We introduce NEO-Bench, a multi-source benchmark containing 8,376 images from five astronomical-image datasets. The sources include the Hubble Space Telescope, a Stellina smart telescope, the United Arab Emirates Meteor Monitoring Network, a TETRA1 telescope using a Celestron C14 with Fastar, and the Roboflow Asteroid dataset. We converted the data to a common YOLO format, audited a sample of labels, and defined within-source and leave-one-source-out evaluation protocols. We evaluated four approaches: Hough, Radon, Gaussian PSF, and YOLO26L. Leave-one-source-out F1 decreased in 14 of 20 image-level method-source pairs and 13 of 20 IoU@0.50 localization pairs. Across the datasets categorized as medium or hard, F1 decreased in 11 of 12 image-level pairs and 9 of 12 localization pairs. evidence.title: NEO-BENCH: A New Multi-Source Benchmark for Generalizable Astronomical Streak Detection
evidence.abstract: Near-Earth Objects (NEOs) can appear as faint streaks in long-exposure astronomical images. Detecting these streaks across diverse observatories requires methods that remain reliable despite differences in image quality, orientation, sky background, and noise. However, existing detectors are commonly evaluated using data from only one source, providing limited evidence of cross-source generalization. We introduce NEO-Bench, a multi-source benchmark containing 8,376 images from five astronomical-image datasets. The sources include the Hubble Space Telescope, a Stellina smart telescope, the United Arab Emirates Meteor Monitoring Network, a TETRA1 telescope using a Celestron C14 with Fastar, and the Roboflow Asteroid dataset. We converted the data to a common YOLO format, audited a sample of labels, and defined within-source and leave-one-source-out evaluation protocols. We evaluated four approaches: Hough, Radon, Gaussian PSF, and YOLO26L. Leave-one-source-out F1 decreased in 14 of 20 image-level method-source pairs and 13 of 20 IoU@0.50 localization pairs. Across the datasets categorized as medium or hard, F1 decreased in 11 of 12 image-level pairs and 9 of 12 localization pairs. These results show that cross-source performance remains inconsistent and that reliable generalization across astronomical imaging sources remains an open challenge. The benchmark, code, and data are publicly available.

title: Continuous vocal-attribute traversals fall below the path resolution of current speech representations: a pre-registered validity gate across three speaker encoders and three neural codecs
abstract: Study 3 of the BedVibe vocal-representation series. Voice conversion, attribute editing and speaker-blend conditioning all move along a straight line between a source and a target point in a learned representation, and treat the intervening coordinates as natural intermediate voices. The path is synthesised, so no ground truth exists anywhere on it except at its two endpoints. This study recorded the path instead. A professionally trained speaker sustains a vowel and slides continuously from clean phonation into rasp, growl or breathiness and back, and from low pitch to high and back — 58 traversals, 2.2–8.5 s each, every intermediate point a real larynx. Two hypotheses and a validity gate with the power to stop the study were pre-registered on 2026-08-14, before any embedding or latent was computed. The gate failed, in both tiers, with zero passes. Across six representations — ECAPA-TDNN, ResNet, WavLM-base-plus-sv, EnCodec, DAC and Mimi — at four window settings and every speaker scope computed, the signal-to-noise ratio of a traversal against the scatter of a steady vowel ranged 0.53–1.85 against a pre-specified requirement of 3.0. A ratio near 1.0 means the displacement produced by a complete vocal transformation is no larger than the displacement observed when the voice is not changing at all. The negative is verified rather than merely observed. Speaker discrimination through the identical code path is positive and rises monotonically with window length in every encoder, so the instrument works. The obvious artifact — phonation attack and decay dominating the endpoint windows — was excluded by re-taking endpoints at 20 % and 80 %, which moved no cell by more than 0.39. The result is a measurement statement about the instruments, and it is quantified: speaker encoders require more audio to produce a stable embedding than a continuous vocal traversal can spare while still resolving its own shape. The two hypotheses are recorded as unreachable with these instruments, not as refuted; no statistic bearing on either was computed. One descriptive observation is reported separately and explicitly outside the hypothesis frame: at 500 ms under ECAPA, a single speaker sliding from clean phonation into rasp traverses a greater distance in the embedding space than the distance separating two different people producing the same vowel in the same condition (cosine 0.28 versus 0.555). No priority or novelty claim is made anywhere in this paper. The audio is not released with this study.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to topology design utilizing a dynamically adaptive self-building topology structure. Traditional topology design methods often rely on manual design, limiting their adaptability to complex scenarios. Our method leverages an adaptive algorithm to dynamically adjust the topology structure in response to input data and desired target structures, resulting in significantly improved design outcomes. The core mechanism centers around continuous, self-optimizing adjustments to the topology, enabling a more efficient and flexible design process. The paper details the algorithm's implementation, demonstrates its efficacy through illustrative examples, and explores its potential applications.

title: ##拓扑量子纠缠的非线性几何建模
abstract: This paper explores the application of non-linear geometric modeling to the study of quantum entanglement, focusing on the concept of "拓扑量子纠缠"。 We propose a novel framework for understanding and exploiting the non-linear properties of quantum entanglement, utilizing the principles of topological structures to represent and analyze quantum correlations. The core of this work lies in formulating a model that explicitly incorporates the "拓扑量子纠缠" concept, providing a new perspective on how entanglement behaves and potentially facilitates quantum information transfer. We demonstrate the potential of this approach to address challenges in quantum key distribution and improve the robustness of quantum computations. This research investigates the implications of this model for complex quantum systems and their computational challenges.

title: Algorithmic Self-Organization of Complex Parameter Sets
abstract: This paper explores the potential of algorithmic self-organization to generate complex parameter sets for machine learning models, focusing on enhancing resilience to perturbations and maintaining a high degree of self-organization. The core mechanism centers around a feedback loop that continuously assesses the system's internal state, dynamically adjusting parameters to achieve a stable and diverse configuration. We propose a novel system leveraging this feedback loop to improve the robustness and adaptability of machine learning models. The resulting process offers a significant advancement over current optimization techniques, addressing the inherent brittleness often associated with parameter adjustments.

title: Hypergeometric Functions: An Evolutionary Algorithm for Optimization
abstract: Hypergeometric Functions (HFs) have emerged as a powerful tool in mathematical modeling and analysis, particularly in the context of statistical physics and data analysis. This paper explores the application of evolutionary algorithms (EAs) to optimize high-dimensional data distributions, offering a novel approach to enhancing the performance of machine learning models. The core claim is that a specifically designed hybrid EAs can efficiently search for optimal HFs, leading to improved data distribution and enhanced machine learning performance. The paper details the design of the evolutionary algorithm, its mechanism, and its potential impact on machine learning, emphasizing its efficiency and adaptability.

title: 基于动态自适应的图神经网络的节点优化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel node optimization strategy based on dynamic self-adaptive neural networks (DANNs). Traditional node optimization methods often rely on manual design, limiting their adaptability to changing data. We propose a DANN-based approach that dynamically adjusts the connections between nodes during training, leading to improved model performance. The core mechanism involves a self-adaptive adjustment algorithm that continuously monitors and adjusts the network's connections based on the training data's characteristics. This allows the network to learn more effectively and generalize better to unseen data. The proposed method offers a flexible and robust solution for optimizing node connectivity in neural networks.

title: Topological Gradient Descent for Neural Network Training
abstract: This paper introduces Topological Gradient Descent (TGD), a novel optimization algorithm that utilizes topological properties to guide the training of neural networks. Traditional gradient descent methods often struggle with convergence and stability due to local optima and sensitivity to initial conditions. TGD leverages a "Topological Gradient" – a measure of network topology – to steer the optimization process, resulting in improved convergence and increased stability. We present a framework for calculating and incorporating the Topological Gradient into the gradient descent process, demonstrating its effectiveness through theoretical analysis and experimental validation. The core mechanism involves constructing a graph representation of the network and employing a dynamic topological gradient update.

abstract: This paper introduces TDAO, a novel quantum optimization algorithm designed to address the limitations of traditional optimization methods by dynamically adjusting the quantum potential field during the optimization process. title: Neural Network Topology-Driven Dynamic Program Generation
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neuro-inspired programming by leveraging the dynamic topology of neural networks. Traditional neural network modeling often relies on static, fixed architectures, limiting adaptability and learning capabilities. Our method addresses this limitation by employing a system that extracts topological information – including connection strengths, patterns, and local clusters – from simulated neural network activity. This extracted topology is then utilized by generative algorithms, specifically Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) or Genetic Algorithms, to automatically generate dynamic rules controlling neural network behavior. These rules are designed to adapt to new inputs or environmental changes and are continuously optimized through feedback mechanisms. The core innovation lies in treating the neural network as a dynamic system governed by its topology, enabling the creation of programs with enhanced adaptability and learning. The system's ability to dynamically modify neural network behavior offers a significant advancement in neuro-inspired programming and control.

title: Neural Simulation via a Probabilistic Information Theory Framework
abstract: This paper proposes a novel framework for simulating neural networks based on probabilistic information theory. The core idea is to treat neural simulations as processes of probabilistic information handling, leveraging concepts like entropy and mutual information to model synaptic transmission and learning mechanisms. Traditional neural models often rely on discrete mathematical descriptions, which can be overly simplified and lack the nuanced probabilistic behavior observed in biological systems. This work introduces a mechanism for defining the probability distribution governing synaptic transmission and explicitly linking it to learning rules. The resulting model provides a more biologically plausible representation of neural computation, offering potential advantages for understanding and modeling complex neural phenomena. The framework addresses the limitations of existing approaches by incorporating information theory, providing a probabilistic foundation for neural simulation.

title: Quantum Entanglement Reservoir Computing for Complex System Modeling
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to complex system modeling utilizing quantum entanglement as a dynamically configurable reservoir. Traditional recurrent neural networks often struggle with high-dimensional data and capturing complex temporal dependencies. We propose a Quantum Entanglement Reservoir Computing (QERC) framework where system inputs are directly mapped to entangled qubit states. The reservoir's evolution is governed by weak, time-dependent interactions, enabling non-linear mapping and the emergence of rich temporal correlations. The correlated qubit output, upon measurement, directly reflects the system state. This method offers a potentially significant advantage over conventional approaches by exploiting the inherent redundancy and correlations within quantum entanglement, providing a more robust and efficient representation of complex dynamics. The core claim of this work is the utilization of quantum entanglement as a dynamically configurable reservoir to represent complex, high-dimensional system dynamics, bypassing the limitations of traditional recurrent neural networks. The core mechanism involves mapping system inputs directly to entangled qubit states, with reservoir evolution driven by weak, time-dependent interactions, facilitating non-linear mapping and emergent temporal correlations. Measurement of correlated qubit output directly reflects the system state. ---

title: Quantum State Tomography for Hardware Verification of Quantum Computers
abstract: Quantum state tomography (QST) is a fundamental technique for characterizing quantum states, traditionally employed in research laboratories with highly controlled environments. However, the burgeoning field of quantum computing faces the significant challenge of deploying and verifying quantum hardware in the presence of noise and decoherence, characteristics inherent in current Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) devices. This paper proposes an adapted QST algorithm designed to overcome these limitations. The core idea is to systematically reconstruct the density matrix of a qubit or a small quantum system using a series of carefully designed measurements. We address the impact of noise by incorporating error mitigation strategies within the reconstruction process. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through theoretical analysis and conceptual implementation, highlighting its potential to provide a practical and efficient method for hardware verification of NISQ computers. This work establishes a novel approach for characterizing and debugging NISQ hardware, a critical step toward realizing the full potential of quantum computation.

title: Meta-Learning for Domain Adaptation
abstract: Domain adaptation is a crucial technique in machine learning for addressing the problem of performance degradation when applying models trained on one domain (source) to a different domain (target). Traditional domain adaptation methods often rely on large amounts of labeled target data, which is frequently unavailable or expensive to acquire. This paper proposes a novel approach leveraging meta-learning to facilitate rapid domain adaptation. The core idea is to pre-train a model on multiple source domains to acquire generalized knowledge, and then utilize meta-learning algorithms to efficiently adjust the model parameters based on limited target domain data. This approach significantly reduces the reliance on target domain labels and demonstrates improved adaptation performance compared to conventional domain adaptation methods. The key contributions of this work include the integration of meta-learning with domain adaptation and the demonstration of its effectiveness in scenarios with limited target domain data.

title: Probability Logic Reasoning and Uncertainty Computation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel computational model designed to address the challenges of probability logic reasoning and uncertainty computation. Traditional logical systems struggle to effectively incorporate probabilistic information, leading to limitations in solving complex problems where uncertainty plays a significant role. Our approach combines elements from probability logic, fuzzy logic, and Bayesian networks to create a hybrid system capable of handling both logical deduction and probabilistic inference. The core mechanism involves representing knowledge as a network of interconnected nodes, each associated with a probability distribution and a logical value. This allows for the propagation of both logical consequences and probabilistic updates throughout the network. We demonstrate the model's ability to solve problems requiring reasoning under uncertainty, offering a more robust and flexible solution compared to conventional approaches. The key contribution lies in the synergistic integration of these logical paradigms, providing a framework for intelligent systems to navigate situations characterized by incomplete and conflicting information. The model is presented with a focus on its theoretical foundations and conceptual design, providing a basis for future development and implementation. ---

The core claim is that simulating a complex optimization problem's local search process through the QA's annealing process can effectively locate global optimal solutions. The mechanism involves mapping the solution space of an optimization problem onto the annealing path of QA, controlling the annealing rate and path to guide the solution towards the optimal point. This research leverages QA's inherent ability to mimic physical annealing, aiming to enhance optimization efficiency and accuracy. We present a framework for formulating and applying QA to various complex problems, highlighting its potential advantages over traditional optimization methods. This work contributes to the growing field of quantum computing by demonstrating a practical approach to tackling challenging optimization tasks. The results suggest that QA can be a viable alternative for achieving superior performance in specific optimization scenarios.

title: Contextualized Reinforcement Learning with Memory Networks
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has achieved remarkable success in various domains, but its application to complex, long-horizon tasks remains a significant challenge. Traditional RL algorithms often struggle with incomplete or sparse reward signals, leading to slow learning and difficulty in capturing long-term dependencies. This paper proposes a novel approach to contextualized reinforcement learning by integrating Memory Networks (MNs) into the RL agent. The core idea is to enable the agent to store and retrieve relevant experiences from its past, effectively augmenting its experience replay buffer and facilitating the learning of complex, temporally extended tasks. The MN component acts as an external memory, storing state-action-reward tuples alongside contextual information. When the agent encounters a new state, the MN is queried to retrieve relevant past experiences, which are then used to guide the current action selection. We hypothesize that this contextualization of experience will dramatically improve the agent's ability to learn long-horizon tasks by providing a richer representation of the environment and enabling more efficient exploration. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and a conceptual design, outlining the key components and interactions within the system. Future work will focus on implementing and evaluating this architecture in simulated environments.

title: CAROL: Context-Aware Online Learning for Fuzzer Scheduling
abstract: Ensemble fuzzing runs multiple fuzzers on a target while a scheduler allocates CPU time among them. Existing schedulers base these decisions on compact summaries of past performance and rules fixed before a campaign. Our measurements reveal two limitations. First, past-reward summaries do not reliably capture performance evolution: after accounting for estimation noise, agreement between consecutive-window rankings is statistically indistinguishable from within-window self-agreement. Second, predictive signals vary across targets: on eight of nine targets, a weighting learned from the other eight predicts reward worse than one learned on the current target. We introduce CAROL, an online scheduler that uses each fuzzer's current context. Already available to the dispatch loop, this context describes reward trends, waiting and plateau time, reached code, and estimation uncertainty. CAROL uses context in two ways: a domain-guided method detects whether a fuzzer is rising or rotting and applies a phase-specific learning rule, while a learned method predicts reward from 15 context signals and uses predictive uncertainty for online selection. Across nine Magma targets, CAROL triggers more unique bugs than each of three ensemble-scheduling baselines whenever their results differ, and fewer on none. Compared with the strongest baseline for each target, CAROL gains 11.8% and surpasses an oracle that retrospectively selects the best single fuzzer per target. Removing context eliminates the gain, and the additional bugs are concentrated among those the baselines trigger rarely or never. Run unchanged on five widely used C++ programs, CAROL finds 120 previously unknown crashing defects, deduplicated by site, fault, and entry point; all were reported to maintainers through the projects' stated disclosure channels.

title: Title: Epistemic Morphing (EM)
abstract: This paper introduces Epistemic Morphing (EM), a computational framework for evolving mathematical structures – specifically, geometric predicates – through iterative self-reference. EM provides a novel mechanism for creating self-replicating proofs and geometric models, enabling continuous mathematical evolution. The core of the system involves refining a mathematical predicate by applying it to its own output, driving the dynamic system to produce new proofs and geometric models. This approach offers a potential pathway for discovering new mathematical theorems and algorithms by systematically exploring variations and combinations of existing structures. The paper details the EM process, provides an illustrative example, and discusses potential applications and future research directions.

title: Quantum Machine Learning Adaptive Optimizer
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) presents a paradigm shift in computational paradigms, offering the potential for breakthroughs in various fields, including machine learning. This paper explores the application of Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs) to a novel adaptive optimization framework, termed "Quantum Adaptive Optimizer" (QAO). We detail the fundamental principles of QAO, emphasizing its reliance on quantum error correction and quantum entanglement to enhance the optimization process. The core mechanism centers around leveraging QNNs' inherent ability to represent and manipulate complex data through quantum algorithms, allowing for automatic adaptation to evolving problem landscapes. This research investigates the potential of QAO to overcome limitations of classical optimization techniques, particularly in scenarios demanding high precision and resilience in dynamic environments. The paper concludes with a discussion of the challenges and future directions of this innovative approach.

title: Self-Adaptive Quantum Error Correction Protocol for Quantum Entanglement
abstract: Quantum computing promises revolutionary advancements across diverse fields, but its inherent fragility – the susceptibility to decoherence and errors – presents significant challenges. Quantum error correction is crucial for achieving fault-tolerant quantum computation, but traditional methods often struggle with the complex dynamics of quantum systems and the inevitable degradation of entanglement. This paper proposes a novel self-adaptive quantum error correction protocol, designed to mitigate the effects of entanglement loss through dynamic adjustment of error correction strength and strategic entanglement management. We present a framework incorporating a dynamically adaptive error correction scheme, incorporating a tailored entanglement management strategy, and exploring its potential to significantly enhance the reliability of quantum computations. The proposed protocol leverages feedback mechanisms to optimize the correction process, minimizing the impact of decoherence and increasing the fidelity of quantum states. This work contributes to the development of robust quantum error correction strategies, paving the way for more reliable and scalable quantum technologies.

title: Quantum Simulation of Non-Linear Geometry Correction
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum simulation to address limitations in classical geometric modeling, particularly concerning error correction and improved accuracy. We propose a novel geometric correction algorithm leveraging quantum entanglement and superposition to minimize discrepancies inherent in geometric representations. The core mechanism involves a quantum-enhanced adjustment of geometric parameters within the simulation, guided by the principles of quantum geometry. The goal is to develop a method that surpasses the capabilities of traditional approaches, offering a pathway towards more robust and accurate geometric simulations. The paper details the underlying theoretical framework, the proposed algorithm's mechanics, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the algorithm's efficacy in correcting geometric distortions.

title: Title: Dynamic Constraint-Based Graph Embedding for Adaptive Machine Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic constraint-based graph embedding method designed to facilitate adaptive machine learning. Traditional graph embedding techniques often rely on pre-defined structural constraints, limiting the model's flexibility and hindering the ability to automatically generate hierarchical structures. Our approach leverages reinforcement learning to dynamically adjust graph structure during training, optimizing for both accuracy and efficiency. We propose a framework that iteratively constructs graphs, leveraging node features and relationships to guide the learning process. The core of our method is a reinforcement learning agent that evaluates graph structures and adjusts parameters to improve performance. This allows for the creation of adaptive graphs that can better represent the data and improve the performance of subsequent machine learning tasks. The dynamic nature of the graph structure is crucial for handling complex datasets and optimizing for specific problem requirements. The paper details the architecture, training procedure, and evaluation results demonstrating the effectiveness of this dynamic constraint-based approach.

title: Title: Dynamic Constraint-Based Evolutionary Algorithm for Machine Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel evolutionary algorithm, termed the Dynamic Constraint-Based Evolutionary Algorithm (DCBAE), designed to accelerate the learning of machine learning models and improve model performance through adaptive constraint management. Traditional evolutionary algorithms often rely on fixed constraints, limiting the potential for rapid optimization. The DCBAE dynamically adjusts constraints during the learning process, responding to model progress and optimizing for both accuracy and efficiency. This approach addresses the limitations of static constraint systems, offering a more responsive and effective method for training complex models. We present a detailed theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the benefits of the DCBAE in various machine learning tasks.

title: Quantum Entanglement: A Probability Tensor Model
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, presents a significant challenge to classical computational approaches. This paper explores the development of a probabilistic tensor model to represent and simulate the complexities of quantum information processing, aiming to enhance the efficiency of quantum computation. We propose a novel approach utilizing tensor operations to model entanglement measurements, offering a potential pathway to more streamlined and efficient quantum algorithms. The core claim is that the established probabilistic tensor model, when properly implemented, can provide a robust and scalable framework for analyzing and manipulating entanglement, ultimately contributing to increased computational capabilities within the quantum realm.
